steps.text: Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and garlic salt in a shallow bowl. Beat eggs in a separate shallow bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.

Dip zucchini slices into egg, then press into bread crumbs. Add zucchini in a single layer to the skillet; cook until golden brown, about 3 minutes. Flip; cook other side until tender and golden brown. Sprinkle mozzarella over zucchini; cook until cheese melts, 1 to 2 minutes more.
Spoon sauce onto plates; top with zucchini slices.

review.reviewBody: I baked them for around 20 minutes at 375, turning them over halfway through the baking time, but other than that followed the recipe exactly. Served over pasta with the sauce and mozzarella for an easy and quick meal!

This was an awesome idea for either an appetizer or a side dish. I did not fry the zucchini, as I hate to add the extra fat. Instead, I used seasoned Panko bread crumbs for the breading mix and added 1/2 tsp garlic salt & italian seasoning to the crumb mix. I dunked the thinly sliced zucchini in egg, then the crumb mix & laid slices out flat on a baking sheet. I baked the breaded slices in a convection toaster oven at 400 F for 8 minutes per side. I did not add the mozzarella, as I did not think it needed it & I didn't want a soggy texture. They were nice, golden & crispy & I served with a nice marinara...nobody used the marinara (they were delicious just plain). Wonderful new addition to my recipe box...thx Kelli!!!
5/14/15 EDIT: I just made these again as described above, only used egg whites instead of egg & they were even lower fat with minimal change in flavor. I served these with a creamy horseradish sauce & couldn't stop eating them...delicious combination of flavors...thx Kelli!!!

This is an excellent recipe! I have made it many times, but never tried frying it. I always bake it in the oven. But either way is fine because I will use the olive oil no matter what, if by using it to fry or spraying the cookie sheet with olive oil cooking spray. But one idea hit me as I was beginning to make these again: instead of using as a possible side dish or snack, why not make it into a PANINI SANDWICH... Once you're done cooking the zucchini, heat up ur Panini Press, using the bread of your choice, layer some of the fried zucchini on the bread, top the zucchini with the spaghetti sauce or even roasted red peppers and then the mozerrella cheese then top that with other piece of bread. Spray the Pannini Press lightly with olive oil cooking spray (*Note: spray the Pannini press prior to heating). Once Press is heated, put Pannini sandwich on grill, put down other end of press on top of sandwich and grill it until cheese melts and sauce is heated through and to the doneness of how you like your bread... There you go! A nice Fried Zucchini Pannini Sandwich to serve as a meal for lunch using Kelli's recipe!!

I love these! I made them several times. The original recipe was also 5 stars but I did a couple of things different the last few times. First, I didn't mix the parmesan cheese in with the bread crumbs but sprinkled a little on top after frying. Also I breaded a whole bunch at one time and put them on cookie sheets and stacked them up and froze them for a couple of hours and then put them in freezer bags for later use rather than breading them every time I want some. I also use ranch dressing instead of spaghetti sauce and Mozzerella cheese. They taste just like fried zucchini that I used to get at Coco's restaurant in Tucson. Wonderful side dish. UPDATE: I now use only panko bread crumbs. I also add onion powder and some dried parsley to the bread crumbs. I tried to dip them in flour prior to putting them in the egg as some have suggested, but then I had trouble getting the egg to stick to the zucchini. The egg sticks to the zucchini just fine without the flour.

This is one of our favorites. We grow zucchini and fry fresh. I made a few modifications to the recipee. First, instead of plain bread crumbs, use Panko Italian bread crumbs. Next, coat with flower before dipping in egg mixture. Lastly, instead of putting the mozzarella on in the pan, put it on after removing and when all slices are done, put in oven at 375 for a few minutes to melt. This allows you to serve all slices warm.

This is a simple and easy introduction to fried zucchini. I used Italian breadcrumbs, left out the mozzarella cheeze and used my homemade marinara as a dip. I didn't like the idea of sitting the zucchini in the sauce as I feared it might lose crispiness that way. I really enjoyed it. I'll definitely make again (I think I can do better next time).

Wish I had read some of the reviews first as I would have done some of this differently. I agree that 1/4" slices are too thick..I've ordered a mandolin so I can get thinner slices. Will also sprinkle the cheese on once the slices are in the pan rather than mixing it with the Panko. I will probably look for something similar that is baked in the oven instead

Tried this recipe last night and it was outstanding! I used yellow squash and zucchini and baked at 375 for 25 minutes. Other than those changes, everything else was the same. The squash was crispy and well seasoned. Husband says it's a keeper. Will definitely make again! Kudos to Kelli.

It was OK, but a little too much. Try slicing them length ways, brushing a little olive oil on both sides, sprinkle parmesan cheese on them and bake them at 400 degrees for 10 minutes, then broil them for 4-5 minutes until they are golden brown. Salt and pepper to taste.
Good recipe. I always sweat my zucchini with a sprinkle of salt and let them drain before frying. And I find that using Crisco shortening is better for frying - veggies turn out lighter and crisper.
I just used part of the recipe to make fried zucchini and melted some mozzarella on top. Yum!
I cut the zucchini thicker than called for at 3/16" thick. The zucchini was creamy and the breading had a nice crunch. This was a nice recipe!
Loved it! great recipe.
Fantastic. I added a few more spices just because I like it extra flavourful. Will make many times again!

This is the closest I have found to the way they are served in a favorite restaurant. It is very good. I used zucchini from my garden that have a much higher moisture content. Next time I will try store bought zucchini.
Delicious! Only thing I changed was I dipped the pieces in flour first before the egg and breadcrumbs. Will definitely make these again.

I made it but didn't have mozz cheese, so substituted cheddar & monteray jack (combo) & others w/o cheese @ all, also didn't have any spaghetti sauce! So I'm sure it tasted a lot different than it was suppose to, but it was still good!
Just turned out messy and sloppy.
Sounded delicious and looked great, but all of the coating came off in the pan. What a mess!
